name: World communism
summary: World communism is the aim of a classless, moneyless and finally stateless society spanning the whole world, reached through an international working-class revolution. It rests on common ownership of the means of production, planned production for need, the dissolving of national divisions and antagonisms, and a transitional proletarian state that dies out as classes disappear. It is a goal shared across Marxist currents, which divide on how it is to be reached.
scope: The worldwide end-goal and international programme as set out in the founding texts: Marx and Engels' Communist Manifesto (1848), Engels' Principles of Communism (1847), Marx's Critique of the Gotha Programme (1875), Engels' Socialism: Utopian and Scientific and Origin of the Family, with the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy as scholarly guide. It does not take in later strategy (Leninism, socialism in one country, Trotsky's permanent revolution, Maoism), regimes' records or any one International's programme, which have their own entries; where the founding texts are silent the answer is null.

worker-ownership.rationale: The means of production are to be common property of the associated producers, which the Gotha critique calls the co-operative property of the workers themselves; the statement is the same aim on the scale of single enterprises.

public-ownership.rationale: The Manifesto's measures put credit, communication and transport in the hands of the State and extend state-owned factories; Principles has the proletariat concentrate all capital, agriculture and transport in the state's hands.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The Manifesto lists a heavy progressive or graduated income tax among the measures 'pretty generally applicable' in advanced countries, and Principles heavy inheritance taxes, though only as steps toward abolishing private property.

tax-inheritance.rationale: The Manifesto's measure 3 is the abolition of all rights of inheritance and Principles asks for heavy inheritance taxes as an early step.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Engels holds that the anarchy of production for the market causes recurring crises and must give way to social regulation on a definite plan.

central-planning.rationale: Industry controlled by society as a whole and operated according to a plan is the stated form of communist production; Engels calls for social regulation of production upon a definite plan.

production-for-use.rationale: Communist production is to expand until it satisfies the needs of all, replacing production for the sake of private gain.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Capital increases only by exploiting wage labour: Engels describes the means of production as capital turned into means of exploiting human labour-power, and the Manifesto says capital is added to by living labour that gets only a subsistence wage.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Principles says money becomes superfluous once production is in the nation's hands, and Marx states the aim of abolishing the system of wage labour.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The higher phase of communist society inscribes 'to each according to his needs' on its banners.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Principles states that the division of labour as known up to now will completely disappear, and Marx's higher phase ends the enslaving subordination of the individual to it.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The Manifesto opens with the claim that the history of all hitherto existing society is the history of class struggles.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The Manifesto says intellectual production changes its character as material production changes, and ruling ideas are those of the ruling class; the scholarship confirms this materialist core.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Manifesto calls the executive of the modern state a committee for managing the common affairs of the bourgeoisie, and Engels calls the state in all typical periods that of the ruling class and a machine for holding down the oppressed.

state-harmful.rationale: The state is held to be a class instrument that dies out and in the end is a hindrance to production, yet a proletarian state is needed in the transition, so the texts neither call it unnecessary throughout nor harmless.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Marx states that between capitalism and communism lies a political transition period in which the state is nothing but the revolutionary dictatorship of the proletariat; the scholarship notes it is meant as temporary emergency rule.

revolution-justified.rationale: The Manifesto declares that communist ends can be attained only by the forcible overthrow of all existing social conditions, and Principles says communists will defend the proletariat with deeds if it is driven to revolution.

political-violence-never.rationale: The Manifesto says its ends can be attained only by forcible overthrow, and Principles accepts violent revolution if the proletariat is driven to it, although it would prefer a peaceful course.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Principles answers that the revolution cannot take place in one country alone but must come in all civilized countries, since the world market ties them together, and the Manifesto makes united action of the leading countries a first condition of emancipation; later communist currents divided on this.

workers-nation.rationale: The Manifesto says communists bring to the front the common interests of the entire proletariat independently of all nationality, and that working men have no country.

nation-first.rationale: Placing a single country's interests ahead of cooperation contradicts the Manifesto's stress on the common interest of the proletariat of all countries and the ending of hostility between nations.

open-borders.rationale: Principles says nationalities will mingle and dissolve, and the Manifesto says national differences vanish and exploitation of one nation by another ends, a society that could not keep national frontiers.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Principles predicts that nationalities will dissolve themselves in the association of peoples and the Manifesto calls the revolution a radical rupture with traditional ideas, though neither sets out a policy on national culture.

traditional-family.rationale: The Manifesto says the bourgeois family will vanish with capital, and Principles says communism removes the two bases of traditional marriage by educating children communally and ending the dependence of women on men.

religion-illusion.rationale: Principles says communism makes all religions superfluous and brings about their disappearance, and scholars report Marx's view of religion as an illusion-generating painkiller that withers away when material life is emancipated.

separate-church-state.rationale: Marx demands that government and church alike be excluded from any influence on the school and that the workers' party go beyond toleration of religions, to liberate conscience from religion.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Marx says government and church should be equally excluded from any influence on the school, which rules out religious instruction given by the state.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The Manifesto's measure 3 abolishes inheritance rights, and Principles says estate and class distinctions disappear with private property while opposing the rule of aristocracy and absolute or feudal monarchs.

democracy-best.rationale: Principles calls democracy wholly valueless to the proletariat unless it is used at once as a means of measures against private property, so democracy is valued as an instrument, not as the best form whatever voters choose.

collective-farming.rationale: Principles has the proletariat concentrate all agriculture in the hands of the state, set up industrial armies for agriculture and employ proletarians on publicly owned land, and says agriculture is held back by division of land into small parcels.

all-land-state-owned.rationale: The Manifesto's first measure is the abolition of property in land and the application of all rents to public purposes, and Principles expropriates landowners and puts agriculture in the nation's hands.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The Manifesto separates the abolition of bourgeois property in the means of production from the personal appropriation of products, which it says it does not take away.

property-fundamental.rationale: The Manifesto sums up the communist programme in the single sentence 'abolition of private property', and Principles calls its abolition the shortest way to characterize the revolution.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The communists want the means of production concentrated in the hands of the state and then of the association of the whole nation, and the Manifesto treats small property as something industry is already destroying, not an ideal.

socialized-markets.rationale: The Manifesto speaks of the communistic abolition of buying and selling and Principles says the revolution abolishes competition, so markets are not accepted even under common ownership.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The Manifesto's critique of utopian socialism condemns founding isolated phalansteres and Home Colonies and calls such schemes castles in the air; communism is a society-wide association.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The Manifesto centralises credit in a state bank and extends state factories 'in accordance with a common plan', and Principles puts capital and labour at the nation's disposal.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The Manifesto's measure 5 is a national bank with state capital and an exclusive monopoly of credit, which is the opposite of abolishing banking authority and leaving money to the market.

no-central-bank.rationale: The Manifesto's measure 5 centralises credit in a national bank with state capital and an exclusive monopoly.

public-money-creation.rationale: The Manifesto centralises credit in the hands of the state through a national bank with an exclusive monopoly, and Principles has a national bank suppress private bankers.

taxation-theft.rationale: The Manifesto and Principles demand heavy progressive and inheritance taxation as a means to take capital from the bourgeoisie.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The communist programme gives the state the central economic role of owning and planning production in the transition.

unions-good.rationale: The Manifesto records the workers' combinations (trades unions) as the start of their organisation, and says the real fruit of their battles is the ever-expanding union of the workers.

alienated-labor.rationale: The Manifesto says machinery and division of labour have stripped proletarian work of all individual character and charm, making the worker an appendage of the machine; the scholarship develops this as alienated labour.

wages-fall-to-bare-minimum.rationale: The Manifesto says the average price of wage labour is the minimum wage, but in the Critique of the Gotha Programme Marx attacks the iron law of wages in its Lassallean sense, so the founding texts point both ways.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The Manifesto says the bourgeoisie produces its own grave-diggers and that its fall is inevitable, and Engels says the crises show the bourgeoisie incapable of directing the productive forces.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The Manifesto says the bourgeoisie played a most revolutionary part and created more massive productive forces than all earlier generations, and Principles says private property's abolition became possible only once big industry had developed.

labour-priority-over-capital.rationale: The Manifesto contrasts bourgeois society, where living labour is a means to increase accumulated labour, with communist society, where accumulated labour is a means to enrich the labourer.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The Manifesto notes that in bourgeois society those who work acquire nothing and those who acquire anything do not work, and Marx's lower phase distributes by labour contributed.

pay-for-effort.rationale: In the first phase of communist society each producer receives back from society what he gave it, measured by his labour, before the higher phase distributes by need.

abolish-wage-labour.rationale: Marx states that abolishing the wage system means abolishing wage labour, and the Manifesto says there can be no wage labour when there is no longer any capital.

no-transition-to-communism.rationale: Marx says between capitalist and communist society lies a period of revolutionary transformation with a political transition, and Principles says private property cannot be abolished at one stroke.

workers-own-party.rationale: The Manifesto describes the organisation of the proletarians into a class, and so into a political party, and the communists as the most resolute section of the working-class parties.

workers-parties-campaign-reforms.rationale: The Manifesto says the workers force legislative recognition of their interests, as with the Ten Hours' Bill, and that communists fight for the immediate aims of the working class.

parliamentary-road-socialism.rationale: Principles says a peaceful abolition of private property would be desirable and has the proletariat win through a democratic constitution, but the Manifesto says its ends can be attained only by forcible overthrow.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Principles says conspiracies are useless and even harmful and that revolutions are not made intentionally and arbitrarily but follow from conditions independent of the will of parties.

gradual-change.rationale: Principles expects measures to be introduced gradually after the revolution, but communists reject respect for established institutions: the Manifesto calls for forcible overthrow of all existing social conditions.

restore-past-order.rationale: Principles opposes reactionary socialists who want to restore feudal and patriarchal society as striving for something impossible, and the Manifesto calls them reactionary.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The Manifesto says the ruling ideas of each age have ever been the ideas of its ruling class, and that jurisprudence is the will of a class made into law.

universal-morality.rationale: The Manifesto answers the objection that communism abolishes eternal truths by treating ideas and moral views as products of class antagonisms and changing material conditions.

character-from-environment.rationale: The Manifesto says man's consciousness changes with the conditions of his material existence and social life, and Principles expects people to become different human material under communal production.

positive-liberty.rationale: The Manifesto treats bourgeois freedom of buying and selling as hollow for those without property, and Engels describes communism as the leap from the kingdom of necessity to the kingdom of freedom through control over production.

class-collaboration.rationale: The Manifesto says communists never cease to instill in workers the clearest recognition of the hostile antagonism between bourgeoisie and proletariat.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Principles says free competition, once a spur to big industry, has become a fetter to be abolished, and the Manifesto says national hostility ends when exploitation ends, though neither addresses struggle as an engine of progress directly.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Principles says communism turns relations between the sexes into a purely private matter in which society has no occasion to intervene, by ending the property bases of traditional marriage.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Engels describes monogamy as the domination of man over woman, and the Manifesto says the bourgeois sees his wife as a mere instrument of production.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Engels says women's emancipation becomes possible only when women take part in production on a large social scale and private domestic labour becomes a public industry, and Principles ties women's dependence to private property.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Principles and the Manifesto treat big industry as the necessary material basis for communism and credit the bourgeoisie with huge productive forces.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The Manifesto has the proletariat increase the total of productive forces as rapidly as possible and says the bourgeoisie cannot exist without constantly revolutionising production.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Principles says private property can be abolished only when the means of production are available in sufficient quantity, and communism rests on expanded modern productive forces.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The Manifesto says the bourgeoisie rescued a considerable part of the population from the idiocy of rural life, and Principles wants the town and country distinction to disappear.

municipal-property.rationale: The Manifesto and Principles concentrate the means of production in the hands of the nation as a whole, not in local communities.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Communism is the programme itself, and the Manifesto and Principles reject bourgeois and other socialisms as halfway measures that preserve the old society.

social-market-economy.rationale: Principles says bourgeois socialists who propose welfare measures while keeping the market society must be struggled against, because their measures preserve the foundations of existing society.

defeat-communism.rationale: Communists hold the abolition of capitalism as their goal and treat opponents of communism as enemies in the class struggle.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The Manifesto says the first step in the working-class revolution is to raise the proletariat to the position of ruling class, and Marx's transition has the proletariat hold political power.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Manifesto has the communists support in Poland the party that insists on an agrarian revolution as the prime condition of national emancipation, and puts the property question to the front everywhere.

worker-farmer-alliance.rationale: The Manifesto and Principles have the communists support agrarian reformers, the National Reformers in America, and the Polish agrarian revolutionaries, and say small peasants will depend on the proletariat.

state-finances-worker-businesses.rationale: Marx rejects cooperative societies founded with state aid, saying cooperatives have value only as independent creations of the workers, though he wants cooperative production on a national scale by revolution.

work-centre-of-life.rationale: In the higher phase of communist society labour has become life's prime want, and the Manifesto makes equal liability of all to work a transitional measure.

legal-duty-to-work.rationale: The Manifesto's measure 8 is the equal liability of all to work, with industrial armies.

change-traditions-that-no-longer-suit.rationale: The Manifesto says the communist revolution is the most radical rupture with traditional ideas and relations, and that ancient prejudices are swept away as conditions change.

human-decline-since-golden-age.rationale: The Manifesto and Principles see history as a progression of stages through the development of productive forces, with capitalism more productive than all before it, not a decline from a golden age.

opposition-only-legal-channels.rationale: The Manifesto says communist ends can be attained only by forcible overthrow, and Principles says communists will defend the proletariat by deeds if it is driven to revolution.

corporate-influence.rationale: The Manifesto calls the executive of the modern state a committee for managing the common affairs of the bourgeoisie, and Engels says the possessing class rules directly through universal suffrage.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The Manifesto says exploitation of one nation by another will be put an end to as exploitation of individuals ends.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: The Manifesto says working men have no country and the communists stress interests independent of nationality, though the proletariat must first constitute itself the nation.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Scholars report Marx's approval of the Paris Commune's arrangement that public offices be paid at the average worker's wage and circulate through election.

recall-officials.rationale: Scholars report Marx was enthusiastic about regular elections, universal suffrage, the binding mandate and recall as the political form he preferred.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Scholars report Marx's approval of the binding mandate and recall of officials in the Paris Commune.
